Product data sources and snapshot caveats

Walmart listing and product-label snapshots checked October 6, 2026. Prices, ratings, reviews and availability are not live/local guarantees. Serving sizes remain explicit, so grams are compared per labeled serving. No medical target, delivery promise or stock status is simulated.

    Consumer-interest context

    In IFIC’s 2025 Food & Health Survey, 64% of U.S. respondents said they try to consume fiber, compared with 56% in 2021. The 2024 result was also 64%, so this is not a one-year jump.

    IFIC 2025 survey, page 22. This measures U.S. consumer interest, not Walmart customers, Walmart sales, or actual fiber intake.

    For team review

    This early proposal makes one interaction concrete so it can be discussed and tested. Product and design feedback can refine the wording and usefulness; senior engineers can assess data coverage, component reuse and implementation risks before a pilot.

    Pilot, trade-offs and open questions

    Start small: choose one grocery category with reliable product data. Agree on the question, primary measure and guardrails before a controlled pilot.

    Measure the shopper outcome

    • Discovery and successful use of relevant filters
    • Time to a suitable product selection
    • Completed purchases, with add-to-cart as a supporting signal

    Watch the trade-offs

    • No-results and filter-clear rates
    • Nutrition-data coverage and serving-size clarity
    • Header height and product visibility on mobile

    Screen space and serving-size clarity: two selected controls add height, and grams per labeled serving are not a like-for-like comparison when serving sizes differ.

    Questions for reviewers: Is the fiber amount and its serving size clear enough for comparison? How should incomplete or conflicting package data affect the result set?

    Please challenge the wording, data assumptions and smallest useful test. A clearer or simpler approach would be useful feedback.

    Limits: this is a screenshot-informed, static prototype with a small sample catalog. Shopping values are source snapshots. It does not connect to Walmart or establish a usability, conversion or revenue improvement. Production data, accessibility and implementation decisions still need review.

    No retailer connection, customer data, tracking, checkout or real cart. Product photos and names come from public listings. Prices, unit prices and review counts are listing snapshots, not live offers. Sources and caveats are linked below the product list. “Fiber” and “Low cal” use explicit illustrative numeric cutoffs here, not verified Walmart definitions or health claims. This compares package information; it does not set a personal intake target. Other filter labels are context only. The demo resets when the page reloads.
